messages:
Alex G: Heads-up — I opened a docs PR to migrate the function-calling examples to the new structured-output JSON schema. Need quick eyes on: param names, example outputs, and a short note about guardrails. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321 :wave:
Maria P: Thanks Alex. I'll skim for wording. Do we need SDK snippet updates as well or just the plain HTTP examples?
Sam L: If we change the top-level field from `tool_result` -> `toolOutput` we should update SDK snippets. Quick diff I tested locally:
```js
const res = await client.callTool('reranker', { input });
// old: res.tool_result.text
// new: res.toolOutput.text
```
Alex G: Good call. I tried to keep an alias note for backwards compat, but probably better to show the new canonical field and add a migration note.
Tilly D: Small docs nits: 1) add a short example for a union type array (tool returns either {choices: []} or {error: string}) 2) mention parse fallback strategy (validate -> fallback to `raw_text`).
Sam L: For the union example we should show a simple validator snippet:
```ts
function isChoiceArray(obj){ return Array.isArray(obj.choices); }
if (!isChoiceArray(parsed)) { // fallback
  parsed = { raw_text: original };
}
```
Maria P: Also link checker flagged a dead link in the PR to the schema reference — will paste the failing URL in thread after I run it.
docs-ci: Link check failed on PR 4321: https://docs.redwood.ai/specs/old-tool-schema -> 404.
Alex G: Thanks bot. I'll update the link to the new canonical schema: https://docs.redwood.ai/schemas/structured-output-2025.json
Tilly D: Can we add a short blurb under "Guardrails" that recommends explicit required fields for tool outputs used in routing? e.g., `request_id` and `confidence` as recommended. Keeps routing resilient.
Sam L: +1. Also adding a tiny `example_response` block helps SDK writers generate types.
Maria P: I'm going to push a small commit to rename the SDK code examples and add the migration note. Will flag the PR for review when done.
Alex G: Awesome. If someone from eng-runtime (cc @Sam L) can double-check the `confidence` semantics (0-1 float vs percentage) that would be great.
Sam L: It's 0..1 float. I'll add a quick comment in the PR about it.
Maria P: Pushed -> PR updated. Changed examples, fixed link, added guardrails paragraph and a brief migration checklist.
Alex G: Perfect. I'll merge after one more docs review. If anyone wants to add an extra example for function-calling with nested tool outputs, drop it here and I'll fold it in. :thumbsup:
